thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT OPENED: gpu-pool-depletion detected for pool=us-west-2/gpu-a. Severity=P1. Trigger: queue_length > 1200 and throttle rate > 10%
Maria (SRE): getting paged. seeing sustained queue growth starting ~1865431800, CPU/GPU utilization at 98% on several nodes, autoscaler not adding nodes. logs show repeated 'no_scale_action: config_mismatch'
Chris (Runtime): I can see the autoscaler rejecting new allocations. stacktrace: `autoscaler: decision_abort(reason=BatchingConfigMismatch)`. Looks like continuous_batching.window_ms got set to 50 (was 250) in last deploy.
Devon (oncall): I'm taking this. @Maria can you push the incident doc link?
Maria (SRE): https://redwood.internal/incidents/1865432100 - added initial impact table. Quick notes: customer-facing latency spike 95th->P95 3.2s->12.8s, error rate (429 throttle) up to 12% across hosted routes. High risk for Dedicated customers on reserved pools.
incident-bot: on-call alert escalated to Devon (oncall) and OpsRotationBot.
Devon (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching override to restore old defaults, 2) increase pool cap by +2 nodes, 3) route noncritical routes to cheap-fallback-model. Applying step 1 now.
Chris (Runtime): before you change anything, note that the prefix cache TTL was also changed in the same PR (PR #4823). If prefix cache miss rate rose, that would increase KV rebuilds and memory pressure. We should check cache metrics.
Aisha (Eng): I dug into PR #4823 — there was an accidental change `continuous_batching.window_ms: 250 -> 50` and `prefix_cache.ttl_seconds: 300 -> 30`. Looks like a bad default slipped through in canary.
Devon (oncall): executing patch to revert continuous_batching to 250ms. command:```shkubectl -n infra set env deploy/autoscaler CONT_BATCH_MS=250 --record```
Devon (oncall): patch applied. watching autoscaler logs.
Maria (SRE): metric check: prefix_cache_miss_rate spiked from 2% -> 38% over last 10m. KV rebuilds causing GPU memory fragmentation.
Chris (Runtime): autoscaler logs now show `recompute_batch_params` kicking in. But we still see scale decisions blocked by `pool_quota_exceeded` on some AZs. Need temporary capacity bump from infra.
Ryan (Prod): Noted customer page: multiple PLG customers seeing 5x latency, two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, FinTrack) reported degraded throughput. Raising to account success.
Devon (oncall): requesting emergency capacity from infra: @ops-rotation-bot can you bump reserved capacity for pool us-west-2/gpu-a by 2 nodes for 1 hour?
OpsRotationBot: Request submitted to infra-provisioner. ETA ~4m.
Aisha (Eng): while we wait, we should throttle low-priority routes: runbook command: ```http POST https://router.internal/reconfig routes=@lowpriority.json``` lowpriority.json contains traffic weights to route noncritical models to cpu-fallback.
Maria (SRE): doing a temporary removal of heavy routes from the main pool. command: ```curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood/route/scale -d '{"route":"/embeddings/large","concurrency":0}'```
Devon (oncall): infra just reported capacity bump applied. Pool nodes +2. monitoring queue length.
Maria (SRE): queue_length trend is flattening. throttle rate dropping from 12% -> 6% within 2m. P95 latency trending down to 5s.
Chris (Runtime): good. I'm going to revert PR #4823 fully on runtime-configs to restore previous prefix_cache.ttl and batching window. command: ```git revert 4823 && ./deploy-config.sh --env=prod```
Aisha (Eng): deploy started. watch config rollout for canary failures.
Devon (oncall): handoff note for followup: we temporarily increased pool cap and routed low-priority traffic away. Need a postmortem to address CI checks that failed to catch runtime default drift and reintroduce automated canary asserts for prefix_cache metrics.
Ryan (Prod): timeline for customer comms: draft sent to CS, notify AcmeCorp & FinTrack with performance summary and remediation steps.
Devon (oncall): handing off to Maria for on-call wrap. Maria, take it from here and close when PMs/CS confirm notifications sent.
Maria (SRE): taking handoff. I'll add incident severity timeline and RCA notes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Devon (oncall): last check: queue < 150, throttle < 1.5%, P95 ~1.1s. I'm declaring immediate mitigation success. Will keep this thread open for postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status=mitigated, mitigation_summary="reverted batching/prefix-cache changes; temporarily increased pool capacity; rerouted low-priority traffic."
Aisha (Eng): next actions: 1) postmortem doc owner = Aisha, 2) add pre-merge lint that rejects runtime default changes without canary flags, 3) add autoscaler unit test to simulate TTL changes.
